# statusline-tokens

> A Claude Code status line for Windows that adds raw token totals, API-equivalent dollar cost, and rate-limit reset countdowns to the 5-hour and 7-day usage windows. One PowerShell file, no dependencies, MIT licensed.

Claude Code ships a status line that reports rate-limit **percentages** but no token counts and no cost. This project fills that gap by reading the transcript files Claude Code already writes to `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` and summing the `usage` block on every assistant turn.

Repository: https://github.com/Gabriel-Dalton/claude-statusline-tokens
Site: https://claude-statusline-tokens.vercel.app/
License: MIT

## What it renders

```
my-project | main | Opus 5 | 5h 82% (168.2M tok, $127, resets 47m @ 1:50pm PDT) | 7d 25% (412.6M tok, $311, resets 4d6h @ Sun 6am PDT) | fable 61% (resets 4d6h @ Sun 6am PDT) | session 8.2M ($6.18) | ctx 63.0k
```

Eight segments: working directory, git branch, model, 5-hour window, 7-day window, Fable 5 weekly limit, current session, context size. The percentage shifts green to yellow to red as headroom disappears.

## The Fable 5 weekly limit

Claude Code meters premium models on a weekly window separate from the plan-wide weekly limit, shown as its own bar by the `/usage` command and tracked internally as the `seven_day_overage_included` bucket.

**That window is not in the status-line hook payload.** Claude Code builds the hook's `rate_limits` object from `five_hour` and `seven_day` only; the Fable, Opus and Sonnet buckets are live in the same process, parsed off `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` response headers, and none are forwarded. No status line can read it from the hook.

`statusline-tokens` fetches it from `GET /api/oauth/usage` instead — the endpoint `/usage` itself uses — where it arrives as a `limits[]` entry with `kind: "weekly_scoped"` and `scope.model.display_name`. The fetch runs in a detached child process at most once per 15 minutes, so the render path never makes a network call, and an atomically created lock file means many open Claude Code windows still produce one request between them. A percentage older than an hour renders `--%` rather than presenting stale data as current.

## Key facts

- **Platform:** Windows. PowerShell 5.1 or later. No Node, no npm, no dependencies.
- **Network:** one request, to Anthropic's own `api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`, for the Fable 5 weekly limit only — no third-party host, no telemetry, never on the render path. Everything else reads local files. `STATUSLINE_SCOPED_LIMITS=0` disables it and the script makes no outbound requests at all.
- **Install:** clone the repo and run `setup.ps1`, which copies the script into `~/.claude/` and merges the `statusLine` block into `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- **Companion:** `claude-dashboard.ps1` renders a full-screen live view with progress bars, a per-project table, a per-model breakdown and a 24-hour sparkline.

## Why the token number looks impossibly large

The most common reaction is "it says I used 168 million tokens today, that can't be right."

It is right, and roughly **97% of it is cache reads**. Every turn re-sends the entire conversation to the model; those replayed tokens are billed and counted each time.

Measured over one real 5-hour session:

| Category | Tokens | Share |
|---|---|---|
| cache read (conversation replayed each turn) | 164.4M | 97.7% |
| cache write | 3.0M | 1.8% |
| output (words the model generated) | 778.0k | 0.5% |
| input (fresh text sent) | 1.8k | 0.0% |
| **total** | **168.2M** | 100% |

Genuinely new work was 3.8M tokens (2.3%). The confirming arithmetic: 827 assistant turns x 198.8k average context re-read = 164.4M, which matches the measured cache-read total exactly.

`scripts/verify-tokens.ps1` reproduces this breakdown on any machine, using a full JSON parse rather than the status line's regex path, so the two implementations independently cross-check each other.

## Pricing model

Cost is API-equivalent, not a bill. Subscribers on Claude Pro / Max / Team / Enterprise pay a flat fee regardless. Rates per million tokens:

| Family | input | output | cache read | cache write 5m | cache write 1h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5, Mythos 5 | $10.00 | $50.00 | $1.00 | $12.50 | $20.00 |
| Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, 4.5 | $5.00 | $25.00 | $0.50 | $6.25 | $10.00 |
| Opus 4.1, 4.0, Opus 3 | $15.00 | $75.00 | $1.50 | $18.75 | $30.00 |
| Sonnet 5, 4.x | $3.00 | $15.00 | $0.30 | $3.75 | $6.00 |
| Haiku 4.x | $1.00 | $5.00 | $0.10 | $1.25 | $2.00 |

Each turn is priced with the model recorded on that turn, so mixed-model sessions blend correctly. Cache read is 0.1x input, 5-minute cache write is 1.25x, 1-hour cache write is 2x.

## Rate-limit resets

Claude Code passes `rate_limits.five_hour.resets_at` and `rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at` to the status-line hook as a Unix epoch. The script renders each as a countdown plus local clock time and its zone, e.g. `resets 2h14m @ 12:38pm PDT`. Timestamps are held in UTC internally and converted to local time only at render, so the countdown is unaffected by daylight saving transitions; the zone abbreviation is resolved for the reset instant rather than for the present, and zones without a mapped abbreviation print a numeric UTC offset. `STATUSLINE_TZ_LABEL=0` drops the suffix.
